ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a large triangle, with a right-angle symbol marked at the bottom vertex, so the two slanted sides 8.5 and z are the two legs of the right triangle. A line segment y is drawn upward from the bottom right-angle vertex, reaching the upper side, and there is a right-angle symbol at the intersection point, indicating that y is the altitude from the right angle to the hypotenuse. This altitude divides the upper hypotenuse into a left segment x and a right segment 8.8. The left leg is labeled 8.5, and the right leg is labeled z. Reasoning: Let the whole hypotenuse length be c, then c = x + 8.8, so x = c - 8.8. According to the projection theorem for right triangles, the square of each leg equals the whole hypotenuse multiplied by the adjacent projection segment of that leg on the hypotenuse. The hypotenuse segment adjacent to the left leg 8.5 is x, therefore 8.5^2 = c x = c(c - 8.8). So c^2 - 8.8c - 72.25 = 0. Solving gives the positive root c = (8.8 + sqrt(8.8^2 + 4·72.25))/2 = (8.8 + sqrt(366.44))/2 ≈ 13.9713. The hypotenuse segment adjacent to the right leg z is 8.8, so z^2 = c·8.8 ≈ 13.9713·8.8 ≈ 122.9474. Therefore z ≈ sqrt(122.9474) ≈ 11.09.
